verifications.claim: Artemis II mission features the first crewed flight of the SLS rocket and Orion capsule.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Artemis II was the second flight of the Space Launch System (SLS) and the first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft'; R2: 'Artemis II (April 1, 2026) was the first crewed test flight of SLS and Orion.'
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated in primary sources as the first crewed SLS and Orion flight.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission launched on April 1, 2026, for a 10-day lunar flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Launch date April 1, 2026... crewed lunar flyby mission... mission duration 9 days, 1 hour'; R2: 'Artemis II (April 1, 2026) was a crewed lunar flyby mission.'
verifications.reasoning: Exact date and ~10-day flyby confirmed across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Artemis II launch time is April 1, 2026, 6:35 p.m. EDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.claim: Artemis II duration is approximately 10 days.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '9 days, 1 hour, 32 minutes'; R2: '9 days'; multiple: 'approximately 10-day mission'.
verifications.reasoning: 'Approximately 10 days' directly supported by sources describing ~10 days.

verifications.claim: Artemis II mission goal is to test Orion spacecraft systems, crew capability, and safety for future moon landings.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'validate the Orion spacecraft's systems, crew operations, and mission procedures ahead of sustained lunar exploration'; R2: 'test flight supporting subsequent Artemis missions aimed at returning humans to the lunar surface.'

verifications.claim: Artemis II trajectory is a free-return loop around the Moon, passing 4,700 miles above the surface.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'free-return trajectory... Closest approach... 4,067 mi (6,545 km)' and 'approximately 4,607 miles (7,414 km)' in comparison.
verifications.reasoning: Free-return loop confirmed; distance cited as ~4,000-4,600 miles, 4,700 is close approximation but not exact.

verifications.claim: Artemis II crew includes Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover... mission specialist Christina Koch... Jeremy Hansen'.
verifications.reasoning: Exact crew list and roles match.

verifications.claim: Artemis II tests systems for future lunar landings including Artemis IV in 2028.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test flight supporting subsequent Artemis missions aimed at returning humans to the lunar surface'; R2: 'Artemis IV (early 2028) is planned to be the first... lunar landing'.
verifications.reasoning: Directly supports testing for future landings like Artemis IV.

verifications.claim: Artemis program aims to establish a sustainable human presence on the Moon by the late 2020s.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'develop a permanent base on the Moon... yearly lunar landings thereafter [after 2028]'.
verifications.reasoning: Program goals include sustainable presence starting late 2020s.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV in 2028 is planned as the first crewed landing of the Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis IV (early 2028) is planned to be the first... crewed lunar landing'; R9: 'Artemis IV mission would set out in 2028 to land on the moon'.
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated as first crewed landing.

verifications.claim: Artemis program uses lunar experiences to prepare for the first human missions to Mars.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'as a stepping stone to human missions to deeper space... working toward eventual human exploration of Mars'.

verifications.claim: Artemis I in 2022 was an uncrewed test of SLS and Orion.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2/R8: 'Artemis I (November 16, 2022) was the first uncrewed test flight of the SLS, Orion'.

verifications.claim: Artemis II in April 2026 is a crewed lunar flyby.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1/R2: 'Artemis II (April 1–11, 2026) was a crewed lunar flyby mission'.

verifications.claim: Artemis III in mid-2027 is now a low-Earth orbit mission to test systems.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Artemis III (mid-2027)... conduct rendezvous and docking tests in Earth orbit'; R9: 'Artemis III... low-Earth orbit mission to test systems'.

verifications.claim: Artemis IV in 2028 is planned as a human lunar landing.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2/R9: 'Artemis IV (early 2028)... first crewed lunar landing'.
